title: Pseudorandomness from 4-Wise Independence under Constant IO Locality
summary: The broad counterexample does not cover constant-IO-locality rounds; whether negligible distance from 4-wise independence after iteration guarantees pseudorandomness remains open.

formal_statement.body: A main counterexample to the broadest version of the proposed implication does not refute the restricted setting in which each round permutation has constant input locality and constant output locality; in this setting, each input wire influences only a constant number of output wires, and each output wire is influenced by only a constant number of input wires. The open question is whether, for a randomized permutation $P$ satisfying these locality restrictions, negligible distance of its $T$-fold composition $P^T$ from 4-wise independence implies that $P^T$ is a pseudorandom permutation.

scope.domain: Iterated randomized permutations with constant input and output locality, studied for limited independence and pseudorandomness.
assumptions: The distance of the T-fold composition of P from 4-wise independence is negligible.
parameters: P: randomized permutation used in the composition
T: number of times P is composed
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the T-fold composition of P must then be a pseudorandom permutation.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source explicitly labels this statement Conjecture 5, Constant IO Locality, and presents it as a weakened variant not refuted by the paper's main counterexample.
citation_labels: Jesko Dujmovic et al., When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness
